subject: Request: temporary measurement carveout & regional aggregation for p50/p95
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Joanna Lee <ops@blueocean.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary measurement carveout & regional aggregation for p50/p95

Hi Joanna,

Quick note following our runbook review this morning — Blue Ocean's QA load tests last week generated a sustained burst of synthetic traffic that disproportionately affected p95 for the hosted API in us-west-2. The customer-facing latency (real user) is stable, but our p95 measurement window picked up the test traffic and pushed the 95th percentile above the contracted threshold for two brief windows.

We'd like to propose a narrowly-scoped change to how we compute the latency SLOs for your account to avoid penalizing you for scheduled test windows:

- Tag-based exclusion: add an outbound HTTP header X-BO-Test: true (or X-Redwood-Synthetic: true) for synthetic/test traffic; Redwood would exclude these tagged requests from p95 aggregation.
- Regional aggregation: compute p50 per-region (region-level user experience) and compute p95 at the global-customer level after filtering test tags to avoid cross-region contamination from a single region's internal tests.
- Temporary carveout window: allow a one-time carveout for scheduled load test windows (proposed: 72-hour window around your next planned test — e.g., 2026-03-15 00:00 to 2026-03-17 23:59 UTC) while we validate tagging reliability.

I've attached a brief CSV with the observed synthetic traffic spikes and a proposed rollout config (proposed-rollforward.yaml). If you can confirm that Blue Ocean can surface test traffic via a header (or the job will route through a specific IP range we can filter), we can implement the exclusion on our side as a measurement rule and submit the carveout for legal/ops approval.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Joanna confirms tagging approach (header vs IP).
2) Redwood (Rishi) drafts the measurement and telemetry change and the limited carveout window.
3) Legal adds a one-paragraph addendum to the SLO that documents the carveout and the required audit logs.

Thanks — want to keep your production SLAs intact while letting you run realistic tests.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: synthetic_traffic_analysis.csv, proposed-rollforward.yaml
From: Joanna Lee <ops@blueocean.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-09T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary measurement carveout & regional aggregation for p50/p95

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the clear summary. We ran three scheduled soak tests last week; the controller adds an X-BO-Test header already but (surprise) some of our older job runners didn't set it. We can update the runners by 3/12.

Two questions from our side before we move forward:
- We need to see the exact filtering rule Redwood will apply and a sample of the resulting telemetry to verify you won't exclude any production traffic by accident.
- Our security team will want to keep the test traffic traceable; can Redwood keep a separate tag in the audit logs (so we can prove when a request was excluded and why)?

Assuming those are OK, we're open to the temporary carveout on the proposed dates. I'll loop in Mark (legal) if we get to the addendum stage.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Joanna
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Joanna Lee <ops@blueocean.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary measurement carveout & regional aggregation for p50/p95

Hi Joanna — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming that an X-BO-Test header is available (and a plan to update runners by 3/12). Technical details below and a proposed safe rollout: 

1) Filtering rule (what we'll do):
- Redwood will add a measurement rule that drops requests with header X-BO-Test: true from p95 aggregation and from any global rollup used for contractual latency commitments.
- Dropped requests WILL still be processed by the runtime and will remain visible in request logs; they will be tagged in audit logs with reason="synthetic-exclude".

2) Aggregation policy (how we compute):
- p50: computed per-region (us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, etc.) using only non-synthetic (untagged) requests to reflect regional user experience.
- p95: computed at the customer-global level (aggregating regions) AFTER excluding synthetic tags; this avoids a noisy region pushing global p95 during scheduled tests.

3) Rollout & carveout window (operational safety):
- Canary: deploy the measurement rule to a single region (us-west-2) and monitor for 24 hours.
- If canary looks good, enable reporting rule for your account and set a one-time temporary carveout window for 2026-03-15T00:00:00Z through 2026-03-17T23:59:59Z.
- We'll produce a short evidence package (logs showing tag usage + resulting p95 calculation) within 24 hours of the window closing for your security team.

4) Attachments & config: attached proposed-rollforward.yaml includes the exact filter predicate and the audit-log label mapping (reason=synthetic-exclude).

I also recommend we add a small alive-sample (1% of tagged requests) left in p95 reporting for a short validation period so we can verify the tag correctness end-to-end without impacting contractual measurement. If that sounds risky, we can rely on the canned evidence package only.

If you approve, I'll coordinate with Ops to schedule the canary on 3/13 and the customer carveout on 3/15.

—Rishi
Senior Product Manager, Platform SLOs
Attachments: proposed-rollforward.yaml
From: Mark Taylor <mark.taylor@blueocean.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Joanna Lee <ops@blueocean.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-11T10:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary measurement carveout & regional aggregation for p50/p95

Aisha / Rishi —

Legal is OK with a short, narrowly-scoped carveout so long as we have: 1) an audit trail that shows excluded requests and the exclusion predicate, 2) a one-paragraph addendum appended to schedule A of the customer agreement, and 3) a DocuSign acknowledgement from Blue Ocean ops that the tests were scheduled and that tagging was used.

I've attached a draft addendum (slo-carveout-addendum-draft.pdf). Send me the evidence package after the window and we'll sign the DocuSign link Joanna provided.

Mark Taylor
General Counsel, Blue Ocean AI
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Joanna Lee <ops@blueocean.ai>, Mark Taylor <mark.taylor@blueocean.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-11T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary measurement carveout & regional aggregation for p50/p95

Thanks, Mark — and thanks Joanna. We have alignment on the rules and legal requirements. Action items we will execute this week: 

- Redwood: schedule canary in us-west-2 on 2026-03-13; enable measurement rule in canary with 24h monitoring (owner: Rishi).
- Blue Ocean: finish updating legacy runners to emit X-BO-Test header by 2026-03-12 (owner: Joanna).
- Legal: Mark will review and, if OK, we will send the DocuSign addendum for signature before the carveout window (owner: Mark).

I'll upload the evidence package to the shared Drive link and start the DocuSign envelope after canary verification. Planning note: if we detect any unexpected drop of production traffic in the canary, we will abort and revert immediately and contact Joanna.

I'll follow up with the DocuSign link once the addendum is finalized.

Best,
Aisha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: (none)
